name: Gerd
overview: Gastro-oesophageal reflux disease (GERD) occurs when stomach acid flows back into the oesophagus, causing heartburn and regurgitation. Lifestyle changes and acid-suppressing medicines effectively control most cases.
symptoms: Heartburn after meals or when lying down
riskFactors: Alcohol, chocolate, spicy and fatty foods
diagnosis: Upper GI endoscopy if alarm symptoms or refractory disease
Oesophageal pH monitoring in selected cases
treatment: Avoid trigger foods and late meals
prevention: Avoid lying down within 3 hours of eating
emergencySigns: Chest pain with exertion — exclude cardiac cause

faq.question: Can I rely on this Gerd information instead of a doctor visit?
faq.answer: No. This content supports learning and preparation for conversations with qualified healthcare professionals. It is not a substitute for diagnosis or treatment.

faq.question: What should I do if Gerd symptoms worsen suddenly?
faq.answer: Seek urgent medical care, especially if severe pain, breathing difficulty, confusion, or high fever develops.
